title: Throughput-driven HC allocation & pricing sensitivity tool
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet creates a compact, scenario-driven matrix to map throughput demands (tokens/sec and concurrent streams) to headcount (SWE, infra ops, support) and incremental unit pricing levers. The goal is to produce quick decision inputs for Q4 reforecast: if throughput grows by X% or we pursue a microcommitments pricing tier, what headcount and margin outcomes should we expect over a 12-month horizon?

Context / why this exists:
- We are seeing two correlated dynamics: (1) bursty customer usage from new consumer integrations, (2) customers asking for lower committed-unit pricing (micro-commits for SMB) that would pressure unit economics unless offset by efficiency (batching, quantization).
- Finance needs a fast model to assess tradeoffs across hiring cadence, burst-capacity commit (reserved GPU pools), and pricing tiers. This file is intentionally compact (spreadsheet-style) and meant to be iterated.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline MRR mix: 70% Hosted API, 20% Dedicated, 10% Private.
- Avg tokens per request: 350 (chat mix).
- Baseline throughput observed (week of 2026-10-15): 120M tokens/day ~ 1,389 tokens/sec avg, 6,000 tokens/sec P95 during bursts.
- Current unit cost (hosted): $0.0018 per 1k tokens (infrastructure + amortized infra ops).
- SWE fully-burdened cost: $220k/year; Infra engineer: $260k/year; Support engineer: $140k/year.
- Typical onboarding ramp for infra capacity ops: 3 months full productivity after hire.
- Reservation (dedicated) discount vs hosted: 20% less unit infra cost on provisioned workloads but requires headcount/ops overhead.

Scenario table (monthly cadence, 12 months). Columns: ScenarioName, ThroughputGrowth, PeakMultiplier, MicrocommitAdoption, PriceFloorAdjustment, NetUnitCostImpact
HighBurst, 70%, 2.8x, 0.10, -12%, +8%
SteadyUpside, 28%, 1.6x, 0.04, -6%, +2%
MicroCommitPush, 12%, 1.2x, 0.30, -25%, -18%
EfficiencyWin, 34%, 1.4x, 0.06, -10%, -6%

Headcount mapping (quarterly hires recommended):
- Baseline need to support +30% throughput: +2 infra ops, +3 SWE (serving/runtime), +2 Support (customer ops) across Q1.
- For burst-optimized scenario (+70% throughput): +5 infra ops, +8 SWE, +4 Support; reserve 2 additional SRE on-call shifts if bursts >2x baseline concurrently.

Simple cost model excerpt (annualized):
- Example: HighBurst incremental headcount costs = (5 infra * $260k) + (8 SWE * $220k) + (4 Support * $140k) = $1.3M + $1.76M + $560k = $3.62M/year.
- Infrastructure reservation amortization (capex-like): to meet 2.8x peak multiplier, need 40% more reserved GPU capacity -> incremental reservation amortization $1.1M/year.
- Combined incremental cost = $4.72M/year.

Revenue / unit impact (HighBurst):
- If we do NOT change pricing, revenue uplift from throughput alone (70% more tokens) would be roughly +70% topline on token-billed revenue bucket. But unit infra cost goes +8% (from table above) -> margin tightens.
- If we offer microcommit tier to 10% of customers in HighBurst scenario (as assumed), ARR mix shifts and realized blended unit price falls ~4% net. This eats into the headcount offset.

Pricing sensitivity mini-table (blended unit price impact vs adoption):
- Baseline blended unit price: $0.0021 per 1k tokens (includes margins).
- If microcommit adoption = 10% and microcommit price is -30% vs baseline: blended price = 0.9*baseline + 0.1*(0.7*baseline) = 0.97*baseline (-3%).
- If microcommit adoption = 30% at -30% price: blended price = 0.7*baseline + 0.3*(0.7*baseline) = 0.79*baseline (-21%).

Break-even rule-of-thumb (across scenarios):
- Each incremental infra ops hire (blended cost after ramp ~ $65k/quarter) is worth ~30% improvement in reservation/capacity utilization if paired with smart autoscaling + traffic shaping.
- If we can achieve at least 22% unit cost reduction via batching/quantization on the increased workload, the HighBurst incremental spend is recoverable without raising prices.

Sensitivity sweep (quick):
- Variable: microcommit adoption (0%..40%), price delta (-10%..-35%), throughput growth (0%..80%). Output metric: incremental margin delta vs baseline.
- Quick note: combos where adoption >20% and price delta <= -25% are the most damaging absent efficiency wins.

Operational levers to model/test quickly:
1) Tiered reservation: allow customers to buy micro-reservations (small commit blocks) priced ~15% above true reserved cost but below hosted list price. This reduces churn from SMBs while protecting margins.
2) Burst credits: sell burst credits (prepaid token pools) with higher effective price per token but better utilization. Good for peak-heavy customers.
3) Cross-customer batching incentive: grandfather lower unit price in exchange for enabling enhanced batching telemetry (opt-in).
4) Aggressive quantization pilot on non-chat models targeting 18-22% unit-cost reductions on eligible workload.

Tradeoffs / risks:
- Hiring ahead of visible demand increases cash burn and creates utilization risk if customer growth stalls.
- Under-provisioning causes P95 latency SLO breaches and churn; that risk increases non-linearly with peak multiplier.
- Complex tiering increases ops overhead and sales friction. Must model sales uplift vs migration cost.

Actionable next steps (this week):
- Finance: run full sensitivity sweep with actual contract-level cohort data (request CS to attach three largest accounts by token volume). Owner: Ana. ETA: 2026-11-22.
- Product/Serving: prototype micro-reservation pricing ladder (two SKU sizes) and estimate ops overhead. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-11-29.
- Infra/Optimize: commit to a 6-week quantization pilot on 2 candidate models and run controlled A/B for quality/regression. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2026-12-20.

Open questions / notes to resolve:
- How much of observed P95 burst is correlated across customers vs single-account spikes? (Affects reserve sizing). Linked: JIRA-FIN-3312 (request logs sample).
- Should we instrument token-level latency tagging by customer to measure batching gains? Needs SRE/SDK effort estimate.

Appendix: compact CSV to paste into model quickly (columns: month, tokens_m, hosted_rev_k, hosted_cost_k, dedicated_rev_k, dedicated_cost_k, private_rev_k, private_cost_k, total_inc_headcount_cost_k)
2026-11, 120, 250, 216, 60, 48, 20, 18, 0
2026-12, 140, 292, 254, 70, 56, 24, 21, 120
2027-01, 160, 334, 290, 80, 64, 28, 24, 450
2027-02, 180, 376, 328, 90, 72, 32, 27, 820
2027-03, 204, 426, 372, 102, 82, 36, 31, 1200

If you want, I can convert the above into a full-sheet CSV with separate tabs (Headcount Plan / Sensitivity Sweep / Pricing Ladder) and push a cleaned version to the CONF page. For now, this is intentionally concise and approximation-first — use as a discussion artifact.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a live working sheet: please add row-level commentary rather than editing baseline assumptions unless you annotate the change.
- Major numbers (costs, salaries) are rounded for quick sense-making; we'll sync to payroll/GL when we lock hires.

Ravi
(finance)
